verdict.rationale: Glama documents deploying any registry server onto its own hosting with the Gateway placed in front automatically. The resulting endpoint URL is the Gateway, so a client reaches the server's tools through a logged, access-controlled URL with no proxy setup or user-side infrastructure. Server pages also supply pre-filled client config blocks for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and VS Code. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting a client to a Glama-hosted URL, and explicit docs on the hosted endpoint's transport and auth for clients.

support.subject: As a developer, I can point my MCP-compatible client at a hosted remote server URL and reach downstream tools without deploying any infrastructure

citations.quote: Deploy any server from the registry to Glama and we automatically put the Gateway in front of it. No proxy setup, no manual wiring – the endpoint you get is the Gateway.
Every call through this URL is logged, access-controlled, and credential-managed
each server page shows the exact JSON block to paste, pre-filled for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and VS Code
Connect a GitHub repository and Glama builds the image straight from source.
